notes.howBuilt: The sequence follows the statutory Year 2 spelling rules from the National Curriculum (English Appendix 1), ordered so each week's rule builds logically on the one before — sounds first, then suffixes, then apostrophes/homophones, then the Year 2 common exception words. Because your class is strong, the pace is faster than a typical Year 2 scheme: new rules are introduced roughly weekly rather than fortnightly, and each list includes 1–2 challenge words that stretch beyond the minimum (marked with *) — words that follow the rule but are longer or less frequent, so quick finishers still have something to work for.
notes.testFormat: Weekly test format suggestion: 10 spellings + 2 dictation sentences using two of the words in context (tests application, not just recall — bright spellers often pattern-match a word list without being able to use the words correctly).
notes.pacing: Pacing: 36 weeks fits a school year with room for INSET days, assessment weeks, and a settling-in week at the very start. If your year has more teaching weeks, repeat weeks 35–36 as a rolling review, or fold in extra homophones.
differentiation: Challenge words (*) aren't compulsory — use them as the "if you finish early" extension or as the dictation-sentence word, so accuracy under context is tested, not just rote recall.

Consider a "spot the rule" starter each Monday: show the 10 words and ask the children to work out the shared pattern themselves before you name it — this suits children who are ready to reason about spelling rather than just memorise.
For weeks with exception words (28–34), pair each test with one "apply the rule" bonus word that isn't on any list, to check they're generalising rather than memorising a fixed set.
Revisit trickier rules (doubling, drop-e, y→i) briefly in weeks 35–36 dictation sentences, since these are the ones bright children still misapply under time pressure even when they know the rule.
